To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of big data processing systems can be improved significantly by optimizing the computation on a single node and that the scalability of such systems is limited by the communication between the nodes.

we are able to scale up to 512 nodes and that we can execute a SQL query in 1.6 ms on a 512 node system, which is 173 times faster than the best SQL-on-Hadoop solution and 7 times faster than the fastest parallel database.

(1) when the computation on a single node is optimized for a particular workload, the speedup obtain from adding more nodes diminishes, (2) we propose techniques to scale the optimized computation across hundreds of nodes on high bandwidth networks, and (3) we demonstrate the scalability of our techniques on a prototype of a 512-node distributed system, which outperforms state-of-the-art SQL-on-hadoop systems and traditional parallel database systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the scalability limits of distributed data processing systems, and how we can overcome these limits to achieve the best performance possible.
the design and implementation of a scalable system for data analytics that can achieve extreme performance on a single node, and scale to hundreds of nodes.
the following questions: 1) What are the bottlenecks in scaling data-intensive applications to large clusters?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the scalability of a distributed application is limited not by the number of nodes, but by the efficiency of the computation performed by the application on each node.

we find that when computation on each individual nodes is optimized, peripheral tasks such as creating data parts, messaging and synchronisation between nodes diminish the obtainable speedup from adding more hardware nodes.

, when the computation is optimized on efficient, custom hardware, the performance benefits from scaling to many nodes are limited, and that the scalability is further limited by the network bandwidth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can achieve 100x speedup on single-node data analytics, and 100x scalability on 512-node data analytics.
we have demonstrated that it is possible to achieve a high degree of performance on a single node, and then to scale the system to hundreds of nodes with high efficiency.
the performance and scalability bottlenecks for big-data applications are not in the computation itself but rather in the peripheral activities
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for some applications, a single node can outperform hundreds of nodes, and that the network is the bottleneck for scalability.
the scalability of data analytics frameworks may not be limited by the number of nodes, but by the efficiency of computation on each individual hardware node.
a system which can efficiently execute a workload on a single-node can be scaled to a large number of nodes with minimal performance degradation.
